key_insight: The paper presents a spatial symmetry invariance theorem stating that exact three-dimensional Navier–Stokes solutions preserve symmetric initial-flow structure under periodic boundary conditions.
engineering_relevance: Symmetry preservation offers a benchmark for detecting numerical contamination in turbulence simulations used for CFD validation.
method: Derive a spatial symmetry invariance theorem for deterministic Navier–Stokes equations.
Test traditional DNS against the predicted symmetry preservation.
Examine implications for statistical sensitivity and memory of initial conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports rapid symmetry loss in traditional DNS and possible sensitivity of turbulence statistics to initial conditions, but provides no quantitative errors or simulation details.
watch_item: Symmetry loss can flag numerical error, but claims about statistical unreliability and non-ergodicity require scrutiny beyond this symmetry benchmark.
paper_title: Spatial symmetry invariance of three-dimensional Navier-Stokes turbulence
